key_insight: HVAF-sprayed NiCoCrAlY coatings substantially improved hot-corrosion and erosion resistance of additively manufactured Alloy 718, regardless of post-processing condition.
engineering_relevance: This suggests thermal spray coatings can make EB-PBF Alloy 718 parts more durable for high-temperature service where corrosion and particle erosion are critical.
method: EB-PBF Alloy 718 substrates were prepared in as-built, shot-peened, HIP, and shot-peened + HIP conditions, alongside cast Alloy 718 controls.
Samples were coated with NiCoCrAlY using high-velocity air fuel (HVAF) thermal spray.
Performance was assessed under hot corrosion at 650 °C for 1008 h in Na2SO4 and under erosion testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports severe flaky oxide-scale degradation and strong material removal in uncoated samples, while coated samples showed much less oxide damage and similar erosion resistance across all substrate conditions.
watch_item: Results are based on one coating system and the specified hot-corrosion/erosion conditions, so broader applicability to other geometries, environments, or long-term cyclic service needs verification.
paper_title: Investigation of thermal spray coatings on additively manufactured alloy 718 substrates
